messages:
matt: Heads up — after yesterday's parse-refactor deploy (sha: abc123) we're seeing ~+9% p50 on host-side streaming paths. Noticed in canary and a couple prod nodes. Anyone already digging?

ops-bot: deploy: parse-refactor (abc123) rolled to canary @ 2026-03-20T11:02Z by ci/cd

ravi: saw this in traces too. flame shows most time in Tokenize -> chunkAndEmit -> grpc write path. quick top from pprof: 
```
10.2%  tokenization/tokenizer.go:Tokenize
8.9%   parse/stream.go:chunkAndEmit
6.5%   grpc/stream_writer.go:Writev
4.0%   kvcache/manager.go:EvictIfNeeded
```

sasha: interesting — writev numbers went up after the header coalesce tweak. Was that commit part of abc123?

matt: yes, abc123 included: small changes to proto fragment framing + coalesce window for http2/grpc in host parser. Aim was fewer small writes, but p50 increased.

linh: kvcache_evictions spiked around the same time (1m windows): 1.2k -> 5.4k. My hypothesis: parser now holds onto fragments longer which increases working set for KV cache and thrashes hot shard.

ravi: i can reproduce locally with the replay harness (streaming small messages). repro steps: `./harness replay --profile parse --concurrency 60 --seq-len-dist small` — latency reg reproduces reliably.

sasha: can you dump the request pre/post framing payload sizes? might be more prefix bytes making tokens bigger and changing kernel selection heuristics (longer sequences -> different kernel path).

ravi: payload histogram from replay: median fragment size went from 128B -> 520B after coalesce. avg batch size at runtime dropped from ~16 -> ~4 because more requests are split differently.

matt: oh — smaller batches due to split semantics changing. That would hurt batching heuristics for GPU kernel selection. If avg batch_size < batch_hint we might be hitting a slow kernel.

linh: confirmed via trace: kernel_selector picked the non-vectorized path more often post-change. perf counters: vectorized_kernels 72% -> 34% across samples.

sasha: quick fixes to try: 1) revert coalesce window to previous value, 2) force kernel hint for sequences < X to pick the vectorized kernel, 3) tune host pre-tokenize to emit earlier and keep batch sizes up.

matt: i'm going to run a canary rollback for coalesce window first. if that removes regression we know it's the framing change.

ravi: FYI i ran an experiment toggling kvcache.eviction_threshold + increased cache size by 2x on a canary; evictions down 60% and p50 improved ~4% but not all the way.

linh: another datapoint — gRPC writev call count increased (per-conn): previously 3 writes/response -> now 9 writes/response; causing more syscall overhead and net flushes. Might be because chunk boundaries moved.

sasha: for short term: matt roll back coalesce window. medium: we should add an invariant test in replay harness that asserts avg batch_size and vectorized_kernel_ratio don't regress more than X%.

matt: rollback initiated (rolling canary). will monitor. also opened a ticket to add harness invariant: INF-2158.

ops-bot: canary-rollback: parse-refactor (abc123) rolled back on canary @ 2026-03-20T13:05Z by matt

ravi: after rollback p50 in canary back to baseline, kvcache evictions dropped to ~1.4k. writev count back to ~3. Looks like framing/coalesce was the trigger.

matt: cool. follow-ups: - add replay invariant (batch size + kernel ratio) - add unit tests around framing window behavior - consider kernel selector fallback when batch_size < hint (avoid non-vectorized hurt) - add telemetry to surface kvcache_evictions per-deploy

linh: i'll take the telemetry + eviction dashboard. ravi can you own the harness invariant? sasha take kernel selector fallback?

ravi: will do. quick note: in the meantime we can ship a guard in host parser to prevent coalescing that increases fragment median > 256B. cheap stop-gap.

matt: agreed. thanks all. I'll keep thread updated with rollout metrics.
